questions.question:
**Select the word that is opposite in meaning (ANTONYM) to the word given below**

Amalgamate
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 3'** i.e.** 'Dismantle'.**

__
 
• **Amalgamate** refers to combining or uniting to form one organization or structure.(एकीकरण करना)
 
• **It implies** the fusion or merging of different elements, entities, or groups into a unified whole.
 
• **Dismantle** means to take apart or break down into its constituent parts.(विघटन करना)
 
• This term is **generally used** when something that was put together is being separated or taken apart.
 
• This **term is the antonym **of "amalgamate", as it refers to the opposite process.

Therefore, the **correct answer** is: **'Dismantle'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Integrate:** Integration refers to the process of combining or bringing together parts or elements to form a whole. (एकीकृत करना)
 
• **Combine: **It refers to the process of joining or bringing together two or more things to create a unified entity. (जोड़ना)
 
• **Coalesce:** It refers to the process of coming together to form one mass or whole.(एक होना)

questions.question:
Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order.

P. the shape of an egg has been highly regarded for its evolution

Q. the body in the most efficient way, not roll away once laid, is structurally

R. as large enough to incubate an embryo, small enough to exit

S. sound enough to bear weight and be the beginning of life for so many species
questions.solution:
The **correct answer** is **'Option 1'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Here's an explanation of each part:
 
 
• **P -** "The shape of an egg has been highly regarded for its evolution" - This part serves as **a good opening statement** because it introduces the main subject: the shape of an egg.
 
• **R -** "As large enough to incubate an embryo, small enough to exit" - This is **a description that elaborates **on the qualities of the egg's shape mentioned in part P.
 
• **Q -** "The body in the most efficient way, not roll away once laid" - This** continues the description **started in part R, adding more qualities of the egg's shape.
 
• **S -** "Is structurally sound enough to bear weight and be the beginning of life for so many species" - **This concluding part** sums up why the shape of the egg has been highly regarded for its evolution, tying the sentence together neatly.
 
 

Therefore, the **correct sentence arrangement **is: **'PRQS'** i.e. *"The shape of an egg, as large enough to incubate an embryo, small enough to exit the body in the most efficient way, not roll away once laid, has been highly regarded for its evolution, is structurally sound enough to bear weight and be the beginning of life for so many species."*

questions.question:
Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.

He said, “I will go to Indonesia tomorrow”.

options.text: He said that he would go to Indonesia tomorrow.
He said that he would go to Indonesia the next day.
He said that he would be going to Indonesia the next day.
He said he would go to Indonesia by tomorrow.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 2'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **When converting** direct speech into indirect or reported speech, certain rules need to be followed.
 
• For instance, **verb tenses** usually **shift back** in reported speech.
 
• The present tense** becomes **the past tense, future tense **changes** to conditional tense.
 
• **He said that he would go to Indonesia the next day: **This option** correctly converts **"will go" to "would go" and "tomorrow" to "the next day". 
 
• It is a **correct transformation **of the direct speech into indirect speech.

Therefore, the **correct answer** is: *'He said that he would go to Indonesia the next day.'*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• Given this, let's analyze the options:
 
 
• **He said that he would go to Indonesia tomorrow: **This option **incorrectly** retains "tomorrow". In **reported speech,** "tomorrow" should become** "the next day".**
 
• **He said that he would be going to Indonesia the next day:** While this sentence is grammatically correct, it is a slightly more elaborate way of expressing the future in the past. The simpler form ("would go") is usually preferred.
 
• **He said he would go to Indonesia by tomorrow:** This option changes the meaning of the original sentence. "By tomorrow" implies he will go sometime before or at the designated time (tomorrow), which is not what the original sentence says.

• Hence, the correct word is '**makes**.'

questions.question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose ‘No improvement’ as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

The shelf is __too highest__ for me to reach.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'Option 4'** i.e. **'Too high'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **correct improvement** for the underlined part of the sentence "The shelf is too highest for me to reach" is option 4)** "too high".**
 
• The reason being, the use of **'highest' is incorrect **in this context because 'highest' is the superlative form of the adjective** 'high' and is used** when comparing three or more things.
 
• Here, the **sentence is not comparing** the height of the shelf with other shelves.
 
• Instead, the **comparative adjective** 'high' should be used.
 
• **When 'too' is used before an adjective**, it indicates that something is at a higher degree than is desirable, possible, or allowed, which perfectly fits in this context.

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is: *"The shelf is too high for me to reach".*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Let's examine the other options:
 
 
• **"Too highly"** - 'Highly' is an adverb, not an adjective. Adverbs describe verbs, not nouns. Here, we need an adjective to describe the noun 'shelf', so 'highly' is incorrect.
 
• **"More higher"** - This is grammatically incorrect. The comparative form of 'high' is 'higher', so it's unnecessary and incorrect to say 'more higher'.

questions.question:

questions.solution:

__
 
• The bracketed segment in the sentence "The palace was in turmoil because Sikhandi **(had return.)"** is **incorrect** due to the wrong form of the verb **'return.'**
 
• **In this context,** the past perfect tense is appropriate, given that the action of Sikhandi's return occurred before another past action (the palace being in turmoil).
 
• The **past perfect tense** requires** 'had'** followed by the past participle of the verb.
 
• For the verb **'return,**' the past participle is** 'returned.'**

Therefore, the** correct sentence** is: *'The palace was in turmoil because Sikhandi had returned.'*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Have turned: **This is incorrect as it changes the meaning of the sentence. The verb 'turn' does not convey the same idea as 'return.' Moreover, 'have turned' is present perfect tense, which is not appropriate in this past context.
 
• **Was return:** This is incorrect as the form 'was return' is not grammatically correct in English. If the past continuous tense were being used, the correct form would be 'was returning.' However, this tense is not appropriate for the sentence's context.
